meta.homeDescription: A free test that places you on twelve political axes and shows which ideologies, countries, figures and parties sit closest, with honest uncertainty. No account needed.

footer.disclaimer: Spectrum is an interpretation tool. It reads your answers through a model with real limits; it does not measure who you are.
footer.privacy: Your answers stay in your browser unless you choose to save them.

home.sentence: Twelve axes, because politics doesn’t fit on one line.

quick.name: Quick
quick.blurb: A first sketch of where you stand.

standard.name: Standard
standard.blurb: A sharper picture with sturdier confidence.

deep.name: Deep
deep.blurb: The most detailed reading: twelve questions per axis.

home.modesNote: You can extend a shorter test later and keep your answers. What you see here is the whole test: no hidden extra rounds.

stub.phaseNote: This page arrives in phase {phase} of the build.

test.title: Take the test
test.lead: Pick a length. The question count and time are the whole commitment.

question.title: Question {n} of {count}
question.lead: The questions open in the next build phase.

results.title: Your results
results.lead: Your latest result, read from this browser. Nothing about it is in the address bar.

sharedResult.title: A shared result
sharedResult.lead: Someone shared their position on the twelve axes with you.

compare.title: Compare
compare.lead: Overlay a friend’s result on yours, axis by axis.

dashboard.title: Your dashboard
dashboard.lead: Every result you take is kept in this browser, so you can see how your views change over time.

compass.title: Compass
compass.lead: A continuous map of the political space: pick any two axes, or the overall map.

web.title: Ideology web
web.lead: Ideologies linked by similarity, grouped by family.

sandbox.title: Sandbox
sandbox.lead: Move twelve sliders and watch the closest matches change.

ideologies.title: Ideologies
ideologies.lead: Hundreds of political ideologies and traditions, from mainstream to fringe, each with criticisms and sources.

countries.title: Countries and regimes
countries.lead: Modern countries and historical regimes, each placed as of a stated date.

figures.title: Figures
figures.lead: Historical and contemporary political figures. Positions of living people are editorial estimates.

parties.title: Parties
parties.lead: Real political parties with an “as of” date and the ideologies they draw on.

method.title: Method
method.lead: How answers become scores, how matches are calculated, and where the model’s limits are.
method.axesLead: Each axis is independent. You can favour markets and open borders, or collective ownership and tradition. During the test you never see which axis a statement belongs to; that is revealed with your results.

answer.title: Answer
answer.body: React to plain statements on a five-point scale. Not sure? Skip it. A skip is not counted as neutral.

see.title: See twelve positions
see.body: Each axis gets a score and a confidence. Where your answers pull in different directions, the results say so.

explore.title: Explore and track
explore.body: Compare yourself with ideologies, countries, figures and parties, and see how your views move over time.

local.title: Local-first
local.body: Results are saved in your browser. Nothing reaches a server unless you choose encrypted sync.

tracking.title: No tracking
tracking.body: No ads, no analytics, no third-party scripts. No cookies unless you create a profile.

honest.title: Honest uncertainty
honest.body: Matches are spread out, not inflated, and every result shows how confident it is.

neutral.title: Even-handed catalog
neutral.body: Every ideology, mainstream or fringe, gets the same encyclopedic treatment, criticisms included.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: Political views are sensitive. This page explains, in plain words, what is stored, where and for how long.
privacy.now: Today: this site sets no cookies, runs no analytics and stores nothing on a server.

imprint.title: Imprint
imprint.pending: The responsible party will be named here before public launch.

notFound.title: This page doesn’t exist
notFound.body: The address may be mistyped, or the page may have moved.

styleguide.title: Styleguide
styleguide.lead: Every component and state in both modes, for design review. This page is not linked and not indexed.

palette.note: Two colours, swapped between modes. No greys, accents, gradients, shadows, opacity, blur or rounded corners. A CI check rejects any other colour.

type.mono: Interface, labels and numbers: IBM Plex Mono
type.sampleHeadline: Where would you draw the line?
type.sampleBody: Each axis is measured on its own. A position on one says nothing about the others, which is exactly why twelve lines describe a person better than one.

buttons.note: Hover and press invert ink and paper. Focus is a 3px outline with a 3px gap. Disabled is a dashed frame.
buttons.order: Default · hover or press · focus · disabled
buttons.linkSentence: Links are always underlined, like <link>this one</link>, and invert on hover.

inputs.note: Labels sit above fields. Errors are written out and thicken the frame; colour never carries meaning.
inputs.error: Error: type at least two letters.
inputs.consent: I understand that this file contains my political views.

answer.note: Five ruled cells and a separate skip. The chosen answer is inverted and marked [X]; hover inverts too. Keys 1–5 answer.

cells.note: Sections are bordered cells on a 12-column grid. Neighbouring cells share one 2px rule.
cells.cellBody: Content sits in ruled cells instead of floating cards.

table.note: 2px frame and header rule, 1px hairlines. Numbers are right-aligned with tabular figures. Countries appear as ISO codes, never as flags.
table.caption: Example: six anchor ideologies
table.name: Name

nav.note: The current page is inverted and bracketed. Tabs follow the same rule and answer to the arrow keys.
nav.panelRadar: All twelve axes in one shape.
nav.panelMap: The overall map of the political space.

toggle.note: The active word is inverted. The theme switch in the header works the same way.

sliders.note: Black bars on ruled tracks with ticks every 10 points. The bracket above shows the uncertainty range. The slider thumb is a solid block.

overlays.note: Both open instantly. The modal is a native dialog over a halftone screen; Escape closes it.
overlays.modalBody: Overlays have a 2px frame and no shadow. The page behind is covered by a dot screen instead of being dimmed or blurred.

legend.note: Every encoding has a written key. Spectra are told apart by shape plus code, never by shape alone.
legend.solid: Solid line: you, or the first series
legend.dotted: Sparse dots: older steps of your trail
legend.halftone: Halftone: bigger dots, more ideologies nearby
legend.you: You: the circle’s size shows uncertainty, the crosshair marks the point
legend.ghost: Ghost compare: a hollow, dashed outline

strip.note: Twelve two-letter axis codes, grouped by domain.
strip.how: Each code has four squares: the left two belong to the first pole, the right two to the second. One filled square means the entry leans that way, two mean it leans strongly, none means it sits near the centre.

radar.note: Centre = −100, solid inner ring = 0, outer ring = +100 on every axis. First profile: solid line, hatched fill, solid corners. Comparison: dashed line, empty fill, hollow corners.
radar.title: Radar: example profile A against B

compass.note: Static preview of the Phase 4 compass on the anchor catalog: distribution across, state power up.
compass.title: Compass preview: distribution and state power
compass.summary: Halftone dots show where ideologies cluster. One marker per spectrum, your position with its uncertainty circle, three earlier results as a trail, and a friend as a ghost.

web.note: Static preview of the Phase 10 web view: placement from the overall map, each node joined to its two nearest neighbours. Hover over a node to see its name.
web.title: Web view preview: seventeen anchor ideologies

images.note: Photos become 1-bit ordered-dither images at build time. Author, licence and source stay visible under every image.
images.glyphsNote: Each catalog entry gets a symmetric 5×5 pattern derived from its id: original, no symbols, no faces.
images.flagsNote: No flags. Countries are named and coded in text, e.g. CH, DE, FR.
